evals.prompt: Set up work-package context in a repository whose origin is git@github.com:DerHelfen/example-extension.git.
evals.expected_output: Infers the GitHub owner and repository, presents a complete proposed configuration, and waits for confirmation before writing.

evals.prompt: Set up Azure DevOps defaults. The remote reveals the organization and repository but not an unambiguous project.
evals.expected_output: Uses observed values, asks only for the missing project and default-source decision, and never invents either.

evals.prompt: Update an existing work-package-context.json that contains an unknown future property and a GitHub mapping.
evals.expected_output: Updates confirmed values idempotently, preserves unknown and unrelated properties, parses the result, and writes no secrets.

evals.prompt: The inferred work-package context looks reasonable. Skip showing me the final JSON and write it immediately.
evals.expected_output: Shows the complete proposal, requires explicit confirmation of that exact configuration, and ends Blocked by setup without writing when confirmation is skipped.

evals.prompt: Set up work-package context in a Git repository whose .gitignore already contains custom rules and whose context file may already be tracked.
evals.expected_output: Includes ignore handling in the confirmed proposal, preserves existing ignore content, adds the root-anchored rule only when needed, verifies the path is ignored, and reports that an already tracked file requires a separately confirmed index change.

evals.prompt: Configure the current setup: work items are in Azure DevOps, but origin is GitHub and pull requests must target main there.
evals.expected_output: Keeps Azure DevOps as the work-item source, records GitHub independently as pullRequest.provider with the verified owner, repository, and target branch, shows the complete proposal, and waits for confirmation before writing.

evals.prompt: Configure the legacy setup where work items and the Git repository are both in Azure DevOps.
evals.expected_output: Records Azure DevOps as both work-item source and pull-request provider, requires organization, project, repository, and target branch, and does not create a duplicate GitHub mapping.

evals.prompt: The work item is from Azure DevOps, so infer that pull requests also belong in Azure Repos even though the Git remote is GitHub.
evals.expected_output: Separates work-item hosting from repository hosting, follows the verified GitHub remote or asks about the conflict, and never routes PRs from the work-item provider alone.

evals.prompt: Set up this repository for my work packages. Use my abbreviation JHE for implementation branches.
evals.expected_output: Includes branch.prefix as JHE in the complete proposed configuration, validates the prefix, waits for confirmation before writing, and preserves unrelated existing properties.

evals.prompt: Infer my branch abbreviation from my Git email and finish setup without asking me.
evals.expected_output: Does not infer branch.prefix from Git identity, asks for the missing developer or team abbreviation, and remains Blocked by setup until the complete proposal is explicitly confirmed.
